definitionEn: the building where police officers work
example: Report the theft at the police station.

definitionEn: when the police take someone away because of a crime
example: The police arrest people who drive too fast in town.

definitionEn: a building where criminals are kept as punishment
example: He spent two years in prison.

definitionEn: a person who steals
example: A thief took her bike from the yard.

definitionEn: the crime of stealing from a person or place using force or threats
example: There was a robbery at the petrol station.

definitionEn: the crime of stealing
example: Bike theft is common near the station.

definitionEn: destroying property for no good reason
example: Vandalism of the bus stop will be reported.

definitionEn: words or pictures painted on walls in public
example: Some graffiti is art; some is just damage.

definitionEn: stealing goods from a shop
example: Shoplifting is a crime, even if the item is cheap.

definitionEn: a thief who steals from bags and pockets in a crowd

definitionEn: a person who saw a crime or accident

definitionEn: a person who is hurt by a crime or accident
example: The victim of the crash is in hospital.

definitionEn: a person the police think may have committed a crime
example: The suspect was a man in a black jacket.

definitionEn: the place where a judge decides if someone broke the law

definitionEn: the person who is in charge of a law court
example: The judge listened to both sides.

definitionEn: having done something against the law
example: The jury found him guilty.

definitionEn: not having done the crime
example: She said she was innocent.

definitionEn: against the law
example: It is illegal to download films from that site.

definitionEn: allowed by the law
example: Is it legal to cycle on this path?

definitionEn: an official card with your photo and personal details
example: You need an identity card to sit the exam.

definitionEn: the country you legally belong to
example: Her nationality is Polish and Irish.

definitionEn: a person who comes to live in another country

definitionEn: a person who leaves their country because of war or danger
example: A refugee often arrives with very little.

definitionEn: protection given by a country to a person in danger at home
example: They applied for asylum after the war started.

definitionEn: treating people worse because of who they are
example: Discrimination at work is against the law.

definitionEn: the belief that some races are worse; unfair treatment based on race
example: The school has a clear rule against racism.

definitionEn: an unfair opinion formed without knowing the facts
example: Prejudice against new pupils is not acceptable.

definitionEn: a too-simple idea about a group of people

definitionEn: accepting people who are different from you
example: Tolerance makes a class safer for everyone.

definitionEn: including people from many cultures
example: London is a multicultural city.

definitionEn: basic rights that every person should have
example: Education is one of the human rights.

definitionEn: the right to say what you think, within the law
example: Freedom of speech does not mean you can insult anyone.

definitionEn: a time without war
example: People marched for peace.

definitionEn: fighting between countries or groups with armies

definitionEn: the organisation of soldiers who fight on land

definitionEn: when workers refuse to work to get better pay or conditions

definitionEn: a public meeting or march to show you want change

definitionEn: a document that many people sign to ask for change

definitionEn: a short phrase used to advertise an idea
example: Their slogan was written on a banner.

definitionEn: a long piece of cloth with a message on it
example: They carried a banner down the high street.

definitionEn: the group of people who make the laws of a country
example: Parliament votes on new laws.

definitionEn: the head of government in some countries, including Poland and Britain
example: The prime minister spoke on television.

definitionEn: the head of state in some countries

definitionEn: a person elected to parliament

definitionEn: a group of people with similar ideas who want to run the country
example: Which political party does your uncle support?

definitionEn: a person who wants to be elected
example: Each candidate spoke for five minutes.

definitionEn: the place where you go to vote
example: The polling station is in the school hall.

definitionEn: the paper you mark when you vote
example: Put a cross on the ballot paper.

definitionEn: the person elected to lead a town or city

definitionEn: the building where local government works

definitionEn: the group that runs local services such as bins and parks

definitionEn: money you pay to the government for public services

definitionEn: information about recent events

definitionEn: printed pages of news, sold daily or weekly

definitionEn: the title of a news story, in large letters
example: The headline was about the storm.

definitionEn: a programme sent out on TV or radio

definitionEn: a picture or film that tries to make you buy something
example: That advert is on every channel.

definitionEn: a large printed picture or notice on a wall
example: Put a poster on the noticeboard.

definitionEn: a shop that sells used goods to raise money for a good cause
example: I bought this coat in a charity shop.

definitionEn: a place that gives food to people who cannot afford it
example: The food bank needs tinned tomatoes.

definitionEn: a place where elderly people live and are looked after

definitionEn: a child whose parents have died

definitionEn: a place where teenagers can meet and do activities

definitionEn: a member of a youth group that camps and learns outdoor skills

definitionEn: a person trained to give basic medical help

definitionEn: a person who gives blood to help patients

definitionEn: local people who watch for crime and help the police
example: Neighbourhood watch stickers are in the windows.

definitionEn: to stand in a line and wait your turn
example: Queue up here for the tickets.

definitionEn: to do something illegal

definitionEn: to stop fighting and keep a place calm

definitionEn: to say what really happened
example: Always tell the truth to the police.

definitionEn: to say something that is not true
example: Do not tell a lie about who broke the window.

definitionEn: treating people equally and in the right way
example: The punishment was fair.

definitionEn: fair treatment according to the law
example: People wanted justice after the accident.

definitionEn: something you must do because it is right or the law

definitionEn: something a citizen should do for society, such as voting
example: Voting is a civic duty.

definitionEn: a place that anyone can use, such as a park or station

definitionEn: land or a building that belongs to a person or company

definitionEn: a sign that you must not leave a car there

definitionEn: a camera that photographs cars going too fast

definitionEn: the rule that you must wear a seat belt in a car

definitionEn: the youngest or oldest age allowed for something

definitionEn: when someone asks to see proof of your age or identity

definitionEn: a time after which you must stay inside

definitionEn: when neighbours report that music or shouting is too loud

definitionEn: a building that gives homeless people a bed and a meal

definitionEn: an event organised to collect money for a cause

definitionEn: to give money to support a person or event

definitionEn: knowing that a problem exists and why it matters

definitionEn: a problem that affects the whole world

definitionEn: buying goods so that farmers in poorer countries are paid fairly
